# A handler inside a view loop reads the loop's own variable, on bubbletea.
#
# The keyboard path emits a second loop over the same list to find the focused
# iteration, and it took For.Key for the index -- which it is only in the
# two-variable head. In `for var it = items` Key is the element, so the
# activation loop bound `it` to an int while the render loop bound it to the
# string, and the generated Go did not compile. passFocusOrder now gives every
# focus loop an ordinal of its own, so Key is the index in all three heads.
#
# This has to be a compiled run: the interpreter never emits either loop, so
# `--platform none` passes under the bug.

[!exec:go] skip 'go toolchain required'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

output { go { bubbletea } }

component main {
    var items list<string> = ["a", "b"]
    var picked = ""
    var hits = 0

    vbox {
        for var it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { picked = it })
        }
        for items {
            button(text="any", @click { hits += 1 })
        }
        for var i, it = items {
            button(text=it, @click { picked = "{i}:{it}" })
        }
    }
    text(value=picked)
}

func testStartsEmpty(t Test, c main) {
    t.assert(c.picked == "")
    t.assert(c.hits == 0)
}
